es.summary: Alteración del metabolismo de la glucosa que aparece por primera vez durante el embarazo y se resuelve después del parto.
key_points: Se detecta con prueba de tolerancia a la glucosa entre 24‑28 semanas.
Resistencia a la insulina materna aumenta por hormonas placentarias.
Control dietético es primera línea; insulina si la glucosa no se controla.
Riesgo de macrosomía fetal, preeclampsia y parto prematuro.

pathophysiology: El aumento de placentaria de estrógeno y progesterona produce resistencia a la insulina.
El páncreas no logra compensar la resistencia, elevando la glucosa plasmática.
La hiperglucemia materna atraviesa la placenta, estimulando la producción fetal de insulina.
signs_symptoms: Poliuria y polidipsia pueden aparecer, pero a menudo es asintomática.
Fatiga y visión borrosa en casos de hiperglucemia marcada.
diagnostics: Prueba de tolerancia a la glucosa oral: glucosa ≥140 mg/dL a 1 h o ≥120 mg/dL a 2 h.
Hemoglobina A1c <6.5% en embarazo (valor de referencia).
treatment: Dieta controlada en carbohidratos (45‑60% de calorías totales).
Insulina de acción corta o basal si la dieta no controla la glucosa.
complications: Mayor riesgo de diabetes tipo 2 materna a largo plazo.
nursing_care: Evaluar glucosa capilar antes y 2 h después de comidas.
Registrar ingesta de alimentos, actividad física y patrones de micción.
Vigilar signos de hipoglucemia: sudoración, temblor, confusión.
Comunicar resultados anormales al médico de forma oportuna.
patient_teaching: Enseñar conteo de carbohidratos y selección de alimentos de bajo índice glucémico.
Explicar la técnica correcta de punción capilar y registro de resultados.
Informar sobre signos de hipoglucemia y cuándo buscar ayuda.
Reforzar la importancia de asistir a todas las visitas prenatales.

en.summary: Alteration of glucose metabolism that first appears during pregnancy and resolves after delivery.
key_points: Detected with glucose tolerance test between 24‑28 weeks.
Maternal insulin resistance increases due to placental hormones.
Dietary control is first line; insulin if glucose is not controlled.
Risk of fetal macrosomia, preeclampsia, and preterm birth.

pathophysiology: Increased placental estrogen and progesterone produce insulin resistance.
The pancreas cannot compensate for the resistance, raising plasma glucose.
Maternal hyperglycemia crosses the placenta, stimulating fetal insulin production.
signs_symptoms: Polydipsia and polyuria may appear, but it is often asymptomatic.
Fatigue and blurred vision in cases of marked hyperglycemia.
diagnostics: Oral glucose tolerance test: glucose ≥140 mg/dL at 1 h or ≥120 mg/dL at 2 h.
treatment: Controlled carbohydrate diet (45‑60% of total calories).
Short‑acting or basal insulin if diet does not control glucose.
complications: Increased long‑term risk of maternal type 2 diabetes.
nursing_care: Assess capillary glucose before and 2 h after meals.
Record food intake, physical activity, and urination patterns.
Monitor for hypoglycemia signs: sweating, tremor, confusion.
Report abnormal results to the physician promptly.
patient_teaching: Teach carbohydrate counting and selection of low‑glycemic index foods.
Explain correct capillary puncture technique and result recording.
Inform about hypoglycemia signs and when to seek help.
Emphasize the importance of attending all prenatal visits.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for unstable blood glucose level
outcomes: Self‑care knowledge: patient describes dietary plan and glucose monitoring

interventions.action: Monitor capillary glucose before each meal and 2 h after
interventions.rationale: Detect early hyperglycemia and adjust treatment

interventions.action: Educate on balanced diet and carbohydrate counting
interventions.rationale: Reduce glycemic load and improve control

interventions.action: Administer insulin as prescribed and record dose
interventions.rationale: Maintain glucose levels within target range

interventions.action: Assess for hypoglycemia signs and symptoms each shift
interventions.rationale: Prevent acute events that compromise mother and fetus

interventions.action: Coordinate weekly prenatal visits with the obstetrician
interventions.rationale: Ensure timely follow‑up and therapeutic plan adjustment

outcomes: Stable gestational weight within expected ranges

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Detect early fluid imbalance

interventions.action: Offer water and sugar‑free drinks every 1‑2 hours
interventions.rationale: Maintain intravascular volume and prevent dehydration

interventions.action: Assess dehydration signs (skin turgor, dry mucous membranes, tachycardia)
interventions.rationale: Identify complication before it worsens

interventions.action: Teach patient to recognize polyuria and increase fluid intake
interventions.rationale: Promote self‑care and prevention of volume deficit

interventions.action: Report to physician any weight loss >2 kg or dehydration signs
interventions.rationale: Allow insulin adjustment or fluid replacement therapy
